references.text: Describes confession of sin as part of the cleansing process, where the one who has sinned must confess their transgression.
Aaron confesses Israel's sins over the scapegoat on the Day of Atonement; the same Hebrew word for confession (והתודה) is used.
Speaks of confession of sin as a condition for restoring the relationship with God.
The one who confesses and forsakes their sins will find mercy.
Ezra describes the people's confession of their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
Nehemiah confesses Israel's sins, including his own and those of his father's house.
The Israelites confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
David confesses his sin to the Lord and receives forgiveness.
Daniel confesses the people's sins in his prayer.
Confession of sin leads to forgiveness and cleansing from all unrighteousness.
An exhortation to confess sins to one another and pray for one another.
